page: Amazon Web Services r4.8xlarge is a memory-optimized fourth-generation instance configured with 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance features 244.0 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding 7.62 GB of memory per core. It operates on the Xen hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture and includes a 45 MB L3 cache. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics are low, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10%. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression are also weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Conversely, multi-core and memory performance are stable, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores all ranking in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, reaching 61.25 GB/sec for large block uncached reads and 25.91 GB/sec for uncached writes.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and average multi-threaded capabilities, the r4.8xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand high single-thread processing speeds. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis, and multi-threaded data processing. However, it is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or large-scale LLM inference, where its 70B model prompt processing speed is poor.
description: Amazon Web Services r4.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 vCPUs, 16 physical Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 cores, and 244.0 GB of RAM. Running on the Xen hypervisor, this x86_64 server lacks local storage but delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Performance benchmarks indicate a significant tradeoff: single-core CPU execution and single-threaded compression are weak, placing in the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. However, multi-core operations, memory bandwidth, and database performance remain in the average tier. The instance achieves 19.71 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 61.25 GB/sec in uncached large-block memory reads. This profile makes the r4.8xlarge qualitatively cost-effective for memory-heavy, multi-threaded workloads such as database hosting, caching layers, and general memory-intensive enterprise applications, while remaining less optimal for compute-bound or single-threaded tasks.
